version_sensitive_claims: Stripe pins the API version via the Stripe-Version HTTP header, NOT a query parameter
Stripe version names are dates with a release suffix (e.g. 2026-06-24.dahlia); older date-only form still valid
A request's version can be overridden per-request (Stripe-Version header / SDK per-call option)
A webhook endpoint can carry its OWN api_version, independent of the account default (falls back to account default when null)
Stripe keeps every previously released version; accounts stay pinned until they explicitly upgrade
RFC 8594 defines only the Sunset RESPONSE header (HTTP-date value) and the 'sunset' link relation; the Deprecation header is a separate, non-8594 spec
Deprecation timelines (6-24 months, GitHub ~12-18, Twitter ~6) and 'keep 3-4 versions' are vendor/team policy, not a universal standard
Adding new error codes / enum values is only safe for clients that tolerate unknown values; it is not unconditionally backwards-compatible
